title: Abnormal Psychology Adventure 3: Schizophrenia
welcome_lead: Today you'll explore schizophrenia — symptoms, causes and treatments.
meta_desc: Psychology Abnormal: schizophrenia symptoms, dopamine hypothesis, diathesis-stress and treatment.
final_note: You distinguished positive/negative symptoms and described biological and cognitive explanations.

walkthroughs.body_html:
DSM-5 requires ≥2 symptoms over ≥6 months.

Positive symptoms: hallucinations (often auditory), delusions, disorganised speech.

Negative symptoms: avolition (lack of motivation), alogia (poverty of speech), flat affect, social withdrawal.

Dopamine hypothesis: excess dopamine activity in mesolimbic pathway. Evidence: dopamine agonists (amphetamines) trigger psychosis; D2 antagonists (haloperidol) reduce positive symptoms.

Genetics: Gottesman (1991) MZ concordance ~48%, DZ ~17%; not 100% — environment matters.

Diathesis-stress: a genetic vulnerability is triggered by stress — childhood trauma, urban upbringing, cannabis use.

Treatment: antipsychotics (clozapine for resistant cases), CBT for psychosis targeting beliefs about voices, family therapy reducing expressed emotion (Brown et al., 1972).
